entities.summary:
The Jahn-Teller effect is a fundamental phenomenon in physics and chemistry, characterized by the spontaneous symmetry breaking in molecular and solid-state systems. This effect was first predicted in 1937 by Hermann Jahn and Edward Teller, and it has since been observed in various materials, including transition metal complexes, rare earth ions, and organic molecules.

One of the key consequences of the Jahn-Teller effect is the distortion of molecular or crystal structures, leading to changes in their physical and chemical properties. This effect has been implicated in a wide range of phenomena, from superconductivity and magnetism to ferroelectricity and optical nonlinearity. The Jahn-Teller effect has also been used to explain the behavior of various biological systems, including the structure and function of enzymes and other biomolecules.

The Jahn-Teller effect has had a significant impact on our understanding of the behavior of materials and biological systems. It has been used to explain a wide range of phenomena, from the properties of superconductors to the behavior of enzymes. The Jahn-Teller effect has also been used to design new materials and technologies, including superconducting devices and biological sensors.

The Jahn-Teller effect continues to be an active area of research, with scientists working to understand its mechanisms and implications in a wide range of fields. The effect has been observed in various materials, including transition metal complexes, rare earth ions, and organic molecules, and it has been used to explain a wide range of phenomena, from superconductivity and magnetism to ferroelectricity and optical nonlinearity. As research continues, it is likely that the Jahn-Teller effect will continue to have a significant impact on our understanding of the behavior of materials and biological systems.
